<div align="center">
    <h1>
        Zabbix AD Group Sync Template
    </h1>
    <h4>
        Creating Zabbix user groups and JIT provisioning mappings from Active Directory groups via Zabbix Agent
    </h4>
</div>
<br>
<br>

<!-- *********************************************************************************************************************************** -->
<!-- *** BODY ************************************************************************************************************************** -->
<!-- *********************************************************************************************************************************** -->
## Description
This template keeps the Zabbix user groups and the provisioning mappings of a user directory in
step with one container of Active Directory groups. A Zabbix Agent on a domain-joined Windows host
reads the group list over WMI from the LDAP namespace (`root\directory\ldap`). A dependent item
then compares the list with Zabbix through the Zabbix API: it creates the user groups that are
missing, adds a provisioning mapping for each of them to the user directory (LDAP or SAML with JIT
provisioning enabled) and assigns a role by name - an administrator role to groups matching a
pattern, a default role to the rest.

Nothing is renamed or deleted. Zabbix groups that no longer exist in AD are only reported, and the
first run can be a dry run that shows what would be created without writing anything.

## What is monitored
- **AD groups** - number of groups in the monitored container, with an informational trigger on
  every change.
- **Synchronization result** - user groups created, mappings added, groups still waiting for the
  next run and the run time of the script.
- **Groups without an AD counterpart** - Zabbix user groups that are not in AD any more and are not
  excluded by the ignore pattern.
- **Collection health** - no-data triggers for the AD query and for the synchronization itself, a
  trigger with the message of a failed run, and a warning when the script gets close to the 10-second
  limit Zabbix gives a preprocessing step.

## Requirements
- **Zabbix 7.0 or higher**
- Windows host **joined to the domain**, with **Zabbix Agent or Agent 2 version 7.0 or higher**:
  older agents ignore the item timeout and give up after their own 3 seconds, which a directory
  query may exceed
- The agent service runs under an account that can read the directory; the default LocalSystem
  account of a domain member can
- A Zabbix API token of a user with the **Super admin** role (the script creates user groups and
  updates the user directory)
- A user directory (LDAP or SAML) with **JIT provisioning enabled** - the template maintains its
  provisioning groups, it does not create the directory
- The Zabbix server, or the proxy that monitors the host, can reach the Zabbix API URL: the
  synchronization runs as a preprocessing step on the server or proxy, not on the agent

## Setup
All PowerShell commands are for an **elevated PowerShell** (right-click -> Run as administrator) on
the Windows host the template will be linked to. To see which agent is installed:

```powershell
Get-Service "Zabbix Agent*"
```

### 1. Check that the host can read the AD groups
Run the WMI query the master item will run, with the container the template should synchronize.
Keep the `%` wildcards and the `like` operator; the query takes a few seconds on a large container.

```powershell
Get-CimInstance -Namespace "root\directory\ldap" -Query "select DS_name from DS_Group where ADSIPath like '%OU=ZABBIX_Groups,DC=example,DC=com%'" | Select-Object DS_name
```

A good answer is one line per group. An empty answer means the container path does not match:
check the OU and DC parts against **Active Directory Users and Computers**. An error mentioning the
namespace means the host is not joined to the domain; the template cannot work around that.

### 2. Check the agent version
Both agents print their version with `-V`; the first line has to start with 7.0 or higher.

```powershell
& "$env:ProgramFiles\Zabbix Agent 2\zabbix_agent2.exe" -V
```

For the classic agent use `& "$env:ProgramFiles\Zabbix Agent\zabbix_agentd.exe" -V`. An older
agent works, but a slow directory query then ends in **No data** because the agent stops after 3
seconds; upgrade it or raise `Timeout=` in its configuration file.

### 3. Create the API token
In the Zabbix frontend open **Users -> API tokens -> Create API token**. Choose a user with the
**Super admin** role (a dedicated user is best), set an expiry date and copy the token: it is shown
only once. The template stores it in the secret macro `{$AD.SYNC.API.TOKEN}`.

### 4. Check the user directory
Open **Users -> Authentication**, the **LDAP settings** or **SAML settings** tab, and open the user
directory the groups belong to. **Enable JIT provisioning** has to be checked and the directory has
to have a name; the script refuses a directory without provisioning with the message
`user directory "<name>" has JIT provisioning disabled`. Note the name for the next steps.

### 5. Import the template
Download [`template_ad_group_sync_zabbix_agent_7.0.yaml`](./7.0/template_ad_group_sync_zabbix_agent_7.0.yaml)
and import it in **Data collection -> Templates -> Import**. Link it to the Windows host from step 1;
the host needs a Zabbix agent interface because the master item is a passive check.

### 6. Set the macros on the host
Open the host, tab **Macros -> Inherited and host macros**, and change these values:

| Macro | Set it to |
|---|---|
| `{$AD.SYNC.API.TOKEN}` | the token from step 3 |
| `{$AD.SYNC.LDAP.ADSIPATH}` | the container from step 1, with the `%` wildcards |
| `{$AD.SYNC.USERDIRECTORY}` | the directory name from step 4 (leave empty when there is only one) |
| `{$AD.SYNC.API.URL}` | the API URL of your frontend, if it is not `http://localhost/api_jsonrpc.php` on the server |
| `{$AD.SYNC.DRY_RUN}` | `1` for the first run |

### 7. Run it once and read the result
Open the host's items, select **Get AD groups** and click **Execute now**. Then open
**Monitoring -> Latest data**, filter the host and open the history of **Synchronize AD groups**.
It is a JSON document; with the dry run on, `created_groups` and `created_mappings` list what the
next real run will do and nothing has been written yet. **Sync: Last error** has to be empty.

| Sync: Last error says | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `userdirectory.get: Invalid params. Not authorized.` | wrong or expired token | create a new token, step 3 |
| `user directory "..." does not exist` | the name in `{$AD.SYNC.USERDIRECTORY}` differs | copy the name from step 4 |
| `user directory "..." has JIT provisioning disabled` | provisioning is off | enable it in step 4 |
| `role "..." does not exist` | a role macro holds a name Zabbix does not have | check **Users -> User roles** |
| `userdirectory.get: HTTP <status>` with a status other than 200, or a connection error | the server cannot reach `{$AD.SYNC.API.URL}` | set the URL the server or proxy can open |

### 8. Switch the dry run off
Set `{$AD.SYNC.DRY_RUN}` on the host back to `0` and click **Execute now** on **Get AD groups**
again. **Sync: Created user groups** shows how many groups this run created and
**Users -> User groups** lists them. At most `{$AD.SYNC.CREATE.LIMIT}` groups are created per run
(20 by default), so a large container is finished by the following runs;
**Sync: Groups waiting to be created** counts down to 0 as that happens. From now on the
synchronization repeats every `{$AD.SYNC.INTERVAL}`.

### Macros used
| Macro | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `{$AD.SYNC.API.TOKEN}` | Zabbix API token of a Super admin user, secret text | |
| `{$AD.SYNC.API.URL}` | Zabbix API endpoint the script calls | `http://localhost/api_jsonrpc.php` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.CREATE.LIMIT}` | Maximum number of user groups created in one run, `0` = no limit | `20` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.DEBUG}` | `1` logs every API call into the server log at debug level | `0` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.DRY_RUN}` | `1` reports what would be created and writes nothing | `0` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.DURATION.MAX.WARN}` | Run time in milliseconds above which the slow-run warning fires | `8000` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.INTERVAL}` | How often the AD group list is read and the synchronization runs | `1h` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.LDAP.ADSIPATH}` | ADSI path filter of the container holding the groups, with `%` wildcards | `%OU=ZABBIX_Groups,DC=example,DC=com%` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.LDAP.NAMESPACE}` | WMI namespace with the directory classes | `root\directory\ldap` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.NODATA}` | How long the AD group list or the synchronization result may be missing | `2h` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.ORPHANS.MAX.WARN}` | Number of Zabbix groups without an AD counterpart tolerated before the warning | `0` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.ROLE.ADMIN}` | Role given to groups matching `{$AD.SYNC.ROLE.ADMIN.MATCHES}` | `Super admin role` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.ROLE.ADMIN.MATCHES}` | Regular expression selecting the administrator groups, matched against the user group name | `Admin` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.ROLE.DEFAULT}` | Role given to every other synchronized group | `User role` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.TIMEOUT}` | Timeout of the WMI query, applied by agent 7.0 or newer | `10s` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.USERDIRECTORY}` | Name of the user directory to maintain, empty = the first one | |
| `{$AD.SYNC.USERGROUP.IGNORE}` | Regular expression of Zabbix user groups never reported as missing in AD | `^(Zabbix administrators\|Guests\|Disabled\|Internal\|No access to the frontend\|Enabled debug mode)$` |
| `{$AD.SYNC.USERGROUP.PREFIX}` | Optional prefix of the created user group names, for example `AD - ` | |
